title: Settings or development: hand over a testable requirement
goal: Separate correcting a filter from adding report behavior and specify a verifiable engineering task.

prerequisites.text: 1c-enterprise.a 6; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: From a familiar situation to a checkable question
paragraphs: You expected 180 but see 105. Correcting the customer selection is a setting. Asking for “closed requests in a period” requires data and capabilities not offered by the initial report. Describe the difference so an implementer can check the result while preserving the working report.

sections.title: Where to act
paragraphs: Work in a new verified copy of your training service. The main Alpha 30/45=75 control and new independent 50/25/15/35/55=180 customer work are different sets. Overall totals include previous work. Nexus saves your note; the standard report and its variants run in external 1C. Do not open unknown EPF/ERF; renaming a variant adds no features.

sections.title: Competence follows the action
paragraphs: A consultant reproduces workflows, checks settings and explains data. Changing posting algorithms, server rights or storage structure needs the appropriate role and review. Being able to press a command is not authority to apply it. Boundaries matter as much as producing an attractive report.

Selecting Beta instead of Alpha is a settings issue: correct selection gives 75 instead of 15. Requesting period/status absent from the starter is a schema/UI change. Renaming a variant or hiding a row cannot implement it.

sections.title: Reason before acting
paragraphs: Follow the scoped native application route; diagrams are not executable browser code.
Identify the infobase, list and particular record separately. A command, visible text and saved state are different things.

sections.title: How to carry out the worked example
paragraphs: Follow the route in your prepared own copy. This is the worked example; the new task below uses different data. Compare each expectation with your actual reread.
Step 1. Select Beta 1/15 then Alpha 2/75. Record parameters and source numbers. Expected: Reference choice explains the discrepancy.
Step 2. Specify period/status and identify their absence from current quick settings. Expected: Missing behavior named.
Step 3. Specify dates/statuses/units, included identities, empty results, period boundaries, retained work and existing report. Expected: Expectations are explicit.
Step 4. Separate engineer code/tests from your user controls. Supply only synthetic examples, without a real-base upload. Expected: Acceptance plan prepared.
Step 5. This lab implements the requirement, not the software change. A future candidate needs old 75/15 and new-case verification. Expected: Requirement IMPLEMENTED; new behavior PLANNED.

sections.title: Turn requests into testable requirements
paragraphs: Turn “fix the report” into period, document set, expected sum and observed discrepancy. Removing a wrong filter may suffice; an absent model field requires a change request. Classification saves time and prevents hiding a data issue by changing formulas without investigation.

Specify which date represents a request, end-day inclusion, included statuses, empty-set behavior and retained reports. A half-open interval can include the start and exclude the day after the end; agree meaning before implementation. This describes a future change, not a starter-report control.

sections.title: Predict the result
paragraphs: A variant is named “Closed in November”. Did period and status automatically appear in the schema?

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: No. A name adds no fields or selection rules. Check existing capabilities first; specify a requirement and acceptance cases for absent period/status support. It is not an implemented change yet.

sections.title: A handoff includes evidence
paragraphs: Provide a minimal synthetic set, versions, steps, expected/actual and tested hypotheses. State prohibited actions: overwriting source, using real data or running unknown processors. The recipient needs a concrete task, not unsorted screenshots. Retain failed attempts to avoid repeating unsafe experiments.

Provide the synthetic 30/45/15 set, actual identities, current schema/version and expected membership. State constraints: preserve source work, retain requests, keep access controls and use no real data. Engineering verifies code/tests; the consultant retains the user question and independent reconciliation.

sections.title: Context and transitions
paragraphs: Read the path and explain what changes at each step. The diagram does not operate the external application.

sections.title: Check the explanation’s boundary
paragraphs: A specified change is required; a variant name does not implement it.
Specify schema/UI changes and their own tests.

sections.title: Acceptance belongs to outcomes
paragraphs: After a fix, the consultant repeats the user workflow and reconciliation; the developer confirms technical checks. A closed ticket is not full acceptance until the original issue and preservation are verified. Outcomes can be partial: the report is fixed while multi-user rights still await a suitable test environment.

Acceptance repeats Alpha 75/Beta15 and new boundary/status cases. Report partial scope honestly: a working filter does not establish permissions or printing. A closed ticket is not acceptance. Retain source, candidate and checks separately.

sections.title: A new independent task
paragraphs: Specify a new “Closed requests for 8–9 November” requirement on a synthetic copy. Separately correct wrongly selected North 105 to the own customer 180(or 185 after the intended edit): that is a setting. For the future change specify document date, bounds[8 November 00: 00, 10 November 00: 00), Closed status, the intended customer reference, an empty set and preservation of the existing report. Current new requests have New status, so the expected closed set is empty, but this filter is not implemented in the initial schema. Publish nothing and do not present the requirement text as a working feature.
Record a prediction first. After your own attempt reveal the reference and compare the selected record as well as its number.

sections.title: Actual training-service window
paragraphs: The author’s separate training copy continues accepted A6: 9/300. Three 30/45/15 requests are added for the main example; the whole copy is 12/390. The main Alpha 75→80 control uses actual DCS. The new independent customer 180→185 is also checked with a saved variant across three 1C processes. OriginalA6 is unchanged; all 12 identities, A4 note, A5 rows and A6 description persist in the copy. Unknown processors were not executed; period/status support is not implemented.

sections.title: What the result establishes
paragraphs: The author’s separate training copy continues accepted A6: 9/300. Three 30/45/15 requests are added for the main example; the whole copy is 12/390. The main Alpha 75→80 control uses actual DCS. The new independent customer 180→185 is also checked with a saved variant across three 1C processes. OriginalA6 is unchanged; all 12 identities, A4 note, A5 rows and A6 description persist in the copy. Unknown processors were not executed; period/status support is not implemented.
Technical checks do not assess understanding. Distinguish your observations from unperformed steps. Training names, numbers and comments are fictional; no work data is required.
